data.cultural_impact: The name Yelena is of Christian-Greek origin, with connections to the ancient Greek goddess Helios, symbolizing sun and light. The cultural impact of this name is one of radiance, strength, and illumination. It has been favored in many Eastern European countries, especially in Russia, where Saint Yelena of Constantinople is venerated. The name bears the sense of authority, resilience, and warmth - qualities highly regarded in many Christian cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: As a Christian name, Yelena holds a significant spiritual significance. Saint Yelena, also known as St. Helen, is the Patron Saint of mothers, travelers, and builders. She is remembered for finding and retreiving the True Cross of Christ in Jerusalem. Spiritually, Yelena signifies a person who shines their light and unwavering faith even in the most challenging circumstances. It is a name that evokes a deep sense of faith, determination, and spiritual devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yelena, meaning "shining light," embodies the radiant spirit of devotion and hope in Christianity. This name evokes the image of a beacon, illuminating the path for seekers on their spiritual journey.
